body:
Never use a dynamic await-import inside an MV3 service worker bundled by vite.

Vite wraps every dynamic import in a preload helper that calls window.dispatchEvent on its error path. A service worker has no window, so the worker dies with "ReferenceError: window is not defined" — logged from background.js with no hint of which import caused it.

Two fixes, use both: make the import static (check for a real cycle first; usually there is none), and set build.modulePreload = false for the worker's build, since a service worker can never use a modulepreload link anyway. Confirm with: grep -c "vite:preloadError" dist/background.js — it must be 0.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: the import sat inside a v1-to-v2 migration branch that only runs when v1 data EXISTS. Every automated run used a fresh profile and returned before reaching it, so the suite was green while a real upgrade was broken. A code path that only real data reaches is a path no test covers — seed the state it needs, or it is untested. Covered now by spike/e2e-migrate.mjs, which was verified by deliberately restoring the broken code and watching it reproduce the exact reported error.

Observed on Chrome 154, 2026-10-02.
